subject: Supply Chain & Logistics
title: Mega Ships and Scale
description: One-minute skill: Mega Ships and Scale.

hook.text: The largest container ship carries 24,000 boxes. Laid end to end, they'd stretch 150 km.

buildup.text: Ships have grown 1,500% since the first container vessel. Bigger ships mean lower cost per box.

discovery.text: Economies of scale drive this growth—doubling capacity doesn't double fuel, crew, or port fees.

twist.text: Mega ships need deep ports and giant cranes. Many ports can't handle them without costly upgrades.

climax.text: When a mega ship is delayed, the disruption is mega too—thousands of containers stuck at once.

punchline.text: Bigger saves money. Bigger also magnifies mistakes.

quiz.question: Why do container ships keep getting bigger?
options: Lower cost per container through economies of scale
